info.text:
In the 22% bracket? You don't pay 22% on everything.
Federal income tax brackets work in layers: each rate only hits the dollars inside its bracket (IRS, tax year 2026).
Our math: a single filer earning $75,000 in 2026 minus the $16,100 standard deduction = $58,900 taxable.
10% x $12,400 = $1,240; 12% x $38,000 = $4,560; 22% x $8,500 = $1,870. Total: $7,670.
That's 13.0% of taxable income and 10.2% of gross. Same math: about 3.6% effective at $25,000, 7.6% at $50,000, 13.2% at $100,000, 15.0% at $125,000 (single, standard deduction). Federal income tax only: no state tax, payroll (FICA) tax or credits.
Sources: IRS IR-2025-103 and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (2026 brackets and standard deduction).
News and education, not financial advice.
